title: Encapsulated Cell Technology for the Delivery of Biologics to the Mouse Eye
protocol: Generate human retinal pigment epithelial cells (ARPE-19) cell line stably expressing the gene of choice according to published protocols.
Maintain cells in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Incubate the cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Replace the medium every 2–3 days.
Passage the cells after reaching 70%–80% confluence using standard tissue culture procedures.
Mix sodium alginate with deionized (DI) water for a final concentration of 2% w/v and purify by filtration with a 0.2 µm sterile syringe filter.
Prepare the cells to be mixed with the alginate solution by trypsinizing, centrifuging, and washing them with 10 mM HEPES buffered saline solution (pH = 7.4).
Count the cells using a hemocytometer and adjust the final cell concentration to 1 x 10^6 in alginate solution.
Load ~300 µL aliquots of alginate and cells mixture into a 3 mL syringe.
Attach the syringe to a syringe pump.
Pump the solution through a 30 G blunt tip needle to a sterile gelling bath placed in a sterile 50 mL beaker below the syringe tip at 7 mm for a needle to bath spraying distance.
Prepare the gelling bath containing 40 mL of 10 mM HEPES buffered saline with 100 mM CaCl2 and 0.5% w/v poly-L-ornithine (PLO).
Adjust the voltage to 6.0 kV and set the flow rate at 60 mm/h for encapsulation.
Connect the anode wire of the high voltage generator needle tip to the needle using the clip.
Attach the ground clip to the copper wire halfway submerged in the gelling bath.
Prepare one batch of alginate + cell mixture (1 mL) which takes approximately 30 min to produce microcapsules (~25,000).
Wash the formed microcapsules containing cells with washing solution (10 mM HEPES buffered saline with 1.5 mM CaCl2 at pH = 7.4) twice.
Incubate encapsulated cells with 10% FBS supplemented DMEM media in a humidified incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Prepare a sample of 500 μL (~30 microcapsules) after incubation to check cell viability.
Wash microcapsules twice with washing solution.
Stain microcapsules for live-dead viability using calcein AM and ethidium homodimer-1 at final concentrations of 2 µM and 4 µM, respectively.
Add 2 mL of the staining mixture to the encapsulated cells.
Incubate the stained capsules in the dark at room temperature for 30–45 min.
Aspirate the staining solution carefully.
Wash microcapsules twice with washing solution.
Observe and image the encapsulated cells using a fluorescent microscope system.
Generate capsules ranging from 100 to 200 µm.
Dilute the generated capsules in serum-free media.
Carefully pull up the diluted capsules into a Hamilton syringe.
Slowly eject 1 μL drops containing capsules onto a microscope slide.
Determine the integrity of the capsules using an upright bright-field microscope.
Adjust voltage and flow rate to produce microcapsules of 150 µm in diameter.
Keep alginate concentration constant while adjusting parameters.
Maintain cells in capsules of appropriate size in serum-free medium.
Determine secretion amount using sensitive ELISAs or western blotting.
Calculate required number of capsules based on PK/PD of the therapeutic.
Inject 10 capsules per mouse eye for optimal efficacy.
Perform intravitreal injections under a dissecting microscope.
Anesthetize mice by intraperitoneal injection of xylazine and ketamine (20 mg/kg and 80 mg/kg) or other preferred anesthetics approved by the specific institution’s Animal Care and Use Committee.
Ensure the appropriate depth of anesthesia using a toe pinch.
Dilate the mouse pupils with phenylephrine HCL (2.5%) and atropine sulfate (1%).
Apply a lubricant eye gel to the eyes to keep them hydrated during the procedure.

Puncture the sclera at the limbus with a 26 G needle as the guide hole, ensuring that the needle is at a 45° angle with the eye and table and the beveled tip is pointed upwards to avoid puncturing the lens.
Carefully inject the capsules using a 27 G blunt-tip needle attached to a Hamilton syringe at a 45° angle under visual inspection, making sure to avoid touching the lens with the needle.
Treat the injection site with antibiotic ointments neomycin and polymyxin B sulfates in addition to dexamethasone ophthalmic antibiotic ointment.
Apply goniotaire hypromellose demulcent ophthalmic solution (2.5%) to both eyes to prevent the corneas from drying out during the recovery period.
Place the mouse on a heating pad held at 37°C and monitor until fully awake.
